(2) u₀ = id gives the same glued function (mark (1/2) = id on U₀), so the marker at U₀ is not needed; the planner's mark (1/2) is kept. (3) The bound a ≤ 1 in the marker family is never used: only a > 3/10 and a ≤ 3/10 are distinguished in cauSep_glue₀₂. causality_follows.survives: Argued, not proved. On ℝ with S = {0}, no separation survives CausalityFollows: there, under CausalityFollows, the conclusion and hcaus, the uniform restart holds. In general (other backgrounds) it is not settled; no reading is decided.
argument: Under CausalityFollows and the conclusion, every development (U, u) has u = u₁ on U, so cau u and C := cau u₁ have the same ≤_N for every N ≤ U. The glued function g of a pair is u₁ on U₀ ∪ U₂. A Cauchy surface of W reads only ≤_N for N ≤ W (CurveOn quantifies over N ≤ W). So 'S Cauchy in U₀ ∪ O for cau g' is 'S Cauchy in U₀ ∪ O for C', and the uniform restart is a statement about C and its Cauchy domains in U₁, as the planner says.

On ℝ with S = {0} every development is an open interval about 0 (hconn, from S Cauchy on a second countable T1 space). A frontier point p of A = U₀ ∩ U₂ in U₂ is an end of U₀ inside U₂, say p = b₀ < b₂. Take O = ]b₀ - ε, b₀ + ε[ ⊆ V with ε < b₀. Then U₀ ∪ O = ]a₀, b₀ + ε[ = W.

W is Cauchy for C. Take c inextensible in W, image J connected. If 0 ∉ J, then J ⊆ ]a₀, 0[ or J ⊆ ]0, b₀ + ε[. In the first case c is a curve of U₀, extensible in U₀ (U₀ Cauchy), and an extension in U₀ is one in W: contradiction. In the second case c is a curve of U₂ (b₀ + ε ≤ b₂, a₂ < 0). An inextensible curve γ of U₂ through its image (exists_inextensible_of_t1_secondCountable) meets 0, since U₂ is Cauchy. γ is monotone: ≤_{U₂} is antisymmetric (hcaus at (U₂, u₂), through CausalityFollows) and curves are continuous (CurveOn.continuousOn). So the piece of γ between 0 and J lies in [0, sup J] ⊆ W, and concatenated with c it strictly extends c in W: contradiction.
Hence on the line the separation needs ¬ CausalityFollows, as the model has. The spacelike premise and V ∩ U₀ ⊆ A are not used.

Why not proved: the concatenation step is not in the library. CurvesExtend gives only image containment (kb/0212), so the extension of c must be built by hand from c and a monotone piece of γ, with the local relation at the junction. Add the monotonicity of curves of a causal open set of ℝ, and it is a module, not a cheap lemma.

Beyond the line: a separation with CausalityFollows needs one causality C whose Cauchy domains of S in U₁ are not closed under 'U₀ ∪ a small O near p', while every Cauchy domain stays GH and tarentin. In smooth Lorentzian geometry ERS's DΣ_V gives the restart at every pair (layer 3, T-loc-quasilinear-slice). In ETT, one route not attempted is a causality on ℝ² whose cones at points near p, outside U₀, are much wider than at p. Each J^±(x) would stay closed while the relation is not (kb/0030). That route is open.

kb_proposals: A solution-dependent causality separates hypotheses that read cau of a glued function. Make cau u the timelike line on a set T of functions not closed under glueSolutions, and the spacelike line off T. Every development then has the timelike line, because a Cauchy surface for the spacelike line contains its open set (Causal.spacelikeLine_subset_of_isCauchySurfaceOn). The glued function of two members of T can fall outside T. Always disclose ¬ CausalityFollows (Causal.Ers482Separation, T-abs-ers-4-82-restart-separation).

spacelikeLine.IsCauchySurfaceOn U S → (U : Set ℝ) ⊆ S (Causal.spacelikeLine_subset_of_isCauchySurfaceOn): through x ∈ U the curve of inextensibleThrough_of_t1_secondCountable is constant by CausalCurveIn.le_of_le and spacelikeLine_le. So {0} is a Cauchy surface of no open set ∋ 0 for the spacelike line.

Pitfall: `simp only [f]` on a def `f := fun u => if u = id ∨ … then … else …` applied to id rewrites `id = id` to True, and `if_pos (Or.inl rfl)` then fails. State the lemma in term mode, `theorem f_id : f id = … := if_pos (Or.inl rfl)`: elaboration unfolds the def definitionally (Causal.Ers482Separation.cauSep_id).

Elsewhere it is open. A separation with CausalityFollows, if one exists, would need a non-closed causal relation near p (one route sketched in causality_follows).
